content.intro: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. In this lesson, focus on older project layouts; then compare it with legacy global state. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use understanding legacy php applications when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. For understanding legacy php applications, begin with older project layouts. Also distinguish legacy global state; mixed presentation and business logic; outdated dependency patterns. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
